correctness.rationale: The full published Eq. (1) and region (2) confirm the mismatch. In the sum of the three living-state equations, incidence cancels and the remaining losses are at least natural mortality. This gives the inward living-state face; the deceased-state equation gives its corresponding inward face. For the last coordinate the forcing is a nonnegative linear form under the stated parameter ranges, including the movement probability in [0,1]. Each living-state simplex has support value max(1,lambda) H_j in the relevant direction, and the deceased-state bound is independently attained. Thus on the proposed upper face the derivative is nonpositive; every strictly smaller constant permits an outward derivative at a feasible boundary state. Together with quasipositivity and local smoothness of Eq. (1), this proves compact positive invariance of the product of living-state simplices and coordinate intervals (the record's 'box'). Independent exact arithmetic for the frozen mathematical counterexample gives bracket 3 and live-only bound at most 2 even under the broader independent-coordinate reading of the typeset maximum, so the old face is outward. The unused coordinates can be set within their own bounds, and the stated H_j and L_1 can be realized by the upstream definitions. The sharpness is for independently feasible states, not for trajectories with fixed initial conditions. No unrelated stability theorem was re-audited; the bundled verify.py was inspected, not executed.
